idiom_name: hand-written renderer functions plus a media-type dispatch table
implementation_notes: Each presentation is a function over the same model struct (fprintf/snprintf into a FILE* or a growable buffer: render_html, render_json, render_csv), and a static table of {media type, renderer} pairs is scanned against the request's Accept header, which replaces both the View hierarchy and the view registry of the classic form. The Observer half is deliberately absent: a C server renders per request, so nothing stays attached to the model; keep the classic attached-observer structure only in an event-loop program (libevent, GTK) that must update several live views, where you need explicit listener lists and invalidation.
pitfalls: snprintf truncates silently: the returned length must be checked and the buffer grown (or the request streamed) or clients receive cut-off bodies.

Escaping is per technology and easy to get wrong: HTML-escape only in the HTML renderer (double-escaping JSON strings corrupts them), and never build JSON with printf - quoting bugs become injection bugs.
Renderers must not retain pointers to per-request buffers or to the shared model across requests; without a DTO copy, a later request's thread can mutate the model mid-render.
